A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SlideAgent work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching relocated material and visually checking redesigned plots.

before.justification: v1 reports original question-answering experiments, retrieval measurements, component ablations and qualitative analyses across proprietary and open-source models.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds MDocAgent comparisons, additional backbone and DocVQA evaluations, failure analysis and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The hierarchical construction, element merging, agent selection, retrieval and answer synthesis procedures are retained. v1 already describes refining global knowledge using page knowledge; v3 clarifies this through initial-versus-refined notation, a single-pass fieldwise rewrite description and a prompt, without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: DocVQA changes from a related-work citation in v1 to an evaluated benchmark in v3 Appendix D.3 and Table 7, substantially extending represented document types to scanned documents, forms and reports. SlideVQA, TechSlides, FinSlides and InfoVQA coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 3 adds MDocAgent comparisons on SlideVQA with GPT-4o and InternVL3-8B backbones. The existing COLPALI, VisRAG, VDocRAG and ViDoRAG comparisons remain. Expanded LLM names match model identities already documented in v1 Table 8.

E3.justification: v3 adds SlideAgent configurations using Gemini-2.5-Flash and Qwen2.5-VL-7B, annotation of 40 failure cases, and a cost comparison separating construction from per-query execution with BM25 or SFR. Existing QA metrics, input handling and temperature settings remain unchanged; the additions do not establish revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v3 introduces a categorized analysis of 40 SlideVQA failures to investigate parsing-related errors, plus computational-cost and scalability analysis comparing retrieval configurations. These address substantial diagnostic and practical questions absent from v1. Existing component-ablation results and the qualitative answer example are retained, with ablation discussion moved into the main text.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix D.4 and Table 8 newly report measurements with ± terms for parsing time, latency, throughput, memory and input tokens. Their statistical meaning and sample or run counts are unspecified. Neither version reports uncertainty estimates or significance tests for the QA accuracy results.

E6.justification: Existing QA tables and component-ablation scores remain unchanged. New results include Gemini/Qwen SlideAgent overall scores of 90.5/80.4, DocVQA scores of 94.5/94.7, and MDocAgent, failure and cost outcomes. BGE's reported MRR gain changes from +2.2 in v1 Table 4 to approximately +0.6 in v3 Figure 6. Absolute retrieval scores and Recall@1/Hit@3 entries are no longer reported.

T1.justification: The bounding-box distance, graph merging and answer-matching mathematics are retained, with no new assumptions, theorems or proofs. v3's refinement equation formalizes an operation already described in v1 rather than introducing substantive new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains query-agnostic hierarchical knowledge with selective global, page and element reasoning. The abstract and introduction retain the same headline gains and model-generalization claims. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets ambiguity, retrieval drift and annotation subjectivity as more frequent failure sources than parsing in its sample, and explains construction-cost amortization. Section 6 replaces v1's explicit absence of element-retrieval evaluation with an annotated-grounding claim, but no distinct grounding protocol or quantitative scores are identifiable. Content-aware initial page selection is also newly proposed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a global-refinement prompt specifying inputs, output fields and overwrite rules, plus parsing and knowledge-construction timing and resource information. It also discloses AI assistance with data processing. Existing parsing tools, thresholds, generation temperature, model identities and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds MDocAgent and briefly discusses multi-agent reasoning with CompanionCast and MASCOT citations; v1's Puffem citation disappears with its user-interaction discussion. The broader research positioning remains stable. Docling and Levenshtein reference revisions identify existing works rather than new additions.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes existing material: it reunites the element-merging explanation previously interrupted by related work, moves ablation interpretations into the main text and ethics into an appendix, and consolidates future work into the conclusion. It also standardizes MLLM terminology and model names and expands the global-refinement explanation.

P2.justification: The retrieval table becomes a four-panel gain plot, query-type bars become radar charts, and ablation plots gain raw-model reference bars with revised axes and styling. v3 adds comparison and error figures and experiment, cost and refinement tables, while moving the query-classification table into the main text and rearranging appendix displays.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens evidence for model and document generalization through its new backbone and DocVQA experiments, while the MDocAgent comparison, error/cost analyses and refinement prompt improve evaluation and practical transparency. Benefits are limited by lost retrieval-score detail, undefined cost uncertainty and the unsupported direct-grounding claim. The retained all-metrics superiority statement also conflicts with Figure 3's newly reported 1.4-point InternVL3-8B F1 loss against MDocAgent.
